Mint 17.3 I presume? I think that uses kernel 3.19, and is built off of Ubuntu, so this https://www.mail-archive.com/ubuntu-bugs@lists.ubuntu.com/msg4848080.html looks like an update is ready for you.

  • Open "Update Manager" (The little shield looking thing in your panel) And run all available updates.

  • After you run the regular updates click on "View" on the Update Managers window.

  • Now click on "Linux Kernels".

  • Scroll down until you see the one that is currently installed and loaded, I think it will be 3.19 but I may be wrong.

  • Now go down a little further until you see the newest most recent update to the current running kernel, it should be 3.19.0-47 (only if you are sure you are currently running 3.19 kernel). Do not install any newer version than what you are currently running, like 4.2, that will likely break your OS.

  • Then click on the new kernel update and select to install it. If all goes well it will download, extract and configure itself in just a few minutes.

  • Then reboot, once rebooted open your terminal and run "uname -a" (without the quotation marks) to check that you are now running the new updated kernel, 3.19.0-47.53.
